objective_pt: Talk about abstract ideas such as freedom, success and happiness: define a concept, use abstract nouns accurately (without "the" for general ideas) and develop an argument beyond personal examples.

teacher.goal_pt: Get the learner to define an abstract concept in their own words.
prompts: What does success mean to you?
Is it the same as happiness?
watchFor: "The success is..." / "The happiness is...": general abstract nouns take no article.
Only giving personal anecdotes, never generalising.

exercises.prompt: Happiness isn't the same thing as success.
accepted: Happiness isn't the same thing as success
Happiness is not the same thing as success
Happiness isn't the same as success

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article: "Happiness is...", not "The happiness is...".
commonErrors.correction_en: Happiness isn't the same thing as success.

options: The freedom is the most important value.
Freedom is the most important value.
A freedom is the most important value.
exercises.explanation_pt: In Portuguese we say "a liberdade", but in English a general abstract idea takes no article: "Freedom is...".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "A educação é a base de tudo."
accepted: Education is the foundation of everything
Education is the basis of everything
Education is the base of everything
Education is the key to everything
Education is at the root of everything
Education underpins everything

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A educação" in a general sense is just "Education" in English, with no article.
commonErrors.correction_en: Education is the foundation of everything.

teacher.goal_pt: Vocabulary for discussing ideas: notion, inherently, subjective, to boil down to, a double-edged sword.
prompts: What does a good life boil down to?
watchFor: "Subjective" stressed on the wrong syllable (it's sub-JEC-tive).

exercises.example_en: The notion of a job for life is disappearing.
In the end, it all boils down to trust.
Technology isn't inherently good or bad.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.pt: dar como certo, não dar valor

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "No fundo, tudo se resume a confiança."
accepted: In the end, it all boils down to trust
Ultimately, it all boils down to trust
At the end of the day, it all comes down to trust
Deep down, it all comes down to trust
Basically, it all boils down to trust
In the end, it all comes down to trust
It all boils down to trust
It all comes down to trust

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Resumir-se a" is "boil down to" or "come down to". "Resume" means "recomeçar" (false friend).
commonErrors.correction_en: In the end, it all boils down to trust.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Trust" here is general and abstract, so no article. Also, "confiança" between people is usually "trust", not "confidence".
commonErrors.correction_en: In the end, it all boils down to trust.

teacher.goal_pt: Word stress in long abstract nouns and adjectives (-ity, -ive, -ical).
prompts: Where is the stress in "-ity" words?
watchFor: Stressing the last syllable as in Portuguese ("responsabiliDADE").
Pronouncing every vowel fully instead of reducing unstressed ones to schwa.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. In "-ity" words, the stress falls just before "-ity": responsiBILity.
accepted: Freedom comes with responsibility

exercises.prompt: It's a subjective, almost philosophical question.
accepted: It's a subjective, almost philosophical question
It is a subjective, almost philosophical question

exercises.explanation_pt: Words ending in "-ity" are stressed on the syllable before it: in-e-QUAL-i-ty.

teacher.goal_pt: Follow an abstract argument and identify the speaker's stance.
prompts: What is the speaker's view of freedom?
watchFor: Losing the thread when there are no concrete examples.
Answering with a story instead of an idea.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What is the speaker's main idea?
exercises.listen: We tend to think of freedom as having more choices, but too many options can actually leave us paralysed and less satisfied.
options: More choice always makes people happier.
Too much choice can reduce satisfaction.
exercises.explanation_pt: The speaker presents the common view and then challenges it: too many options can paralyse us.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and give a short, general definition (not a personal story).
accepted: Success is achieving what you set out to do
Success is achieving your goals
Success means achieving your goals
Success is reaching your goals
Success is doing what you love
Success is being happy with what you do
Success is having a life you're proud of
I'd define success as achieving your goals
I'd say success is being satisfied with your life
Success is feeling fulfilled
For me, success is being at peace with your choices

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "O sucesso" in a general sense is just "Success" in English, without "the".
"Realizar" goals is better as "achieve" or "fulfil". "Realise" usually means "perceber". ("Realise your dreams" exists, but "achieve your goals" is more natural.)

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and say whether you think technology is good or bad, with a nuance.
exercises.listen: Is technology making us more isolated?
accepted: It's a double-edged sword
It's a bit of a double-edged sword
In some ways, yes, but it also connects us
To some extent, but it also brings people together
It can, but it isn't inherently bad
Technology isn't inherently good or bad
It depends on how we use it
It depends on how you use it
Yes and no. It connects us, but it can also isolate us
Partly, but it also connects people

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A tecnologia" in general is "Technology" in English, with no article.
commonErrors.correction_en: Technology isn't inherently good or bad.
It depends on how we use it.

teacher.goal_pt: Develop an abstract argument: define, generalise, give a counterexample, conclude.
prompts: What's the difference between being free and feeling free?
Is there such a thing as a truly selfless act?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "A gente costuma dar a liberdade como garantida."
accepted: We tend to take freedom for granted
We usually take freedom for granted
We often take freedom for granted
People tend to take freedom for granted
We tend to take our freedom for granted
We generally take freedom for granted

commonErrors.explanation_pt: General "liberdade" is "freedom", with no article (or "our freedom").
commonErrors.correction_en: We tend to take freedom for granted.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Dar como garantido" is the fixed expression "take for granted".
commonErrors.correction_en: We tend to take freedom for granted.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Costumar" in the present is "usually" or "tend to". "Used to" is only for the past, and "costume" means "fantasia".
commonErrors.correction_en: We tend to take freedom for granted.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Isso levanta a questão do que realmente significa ser feliz."
accepted: That raises the question of what it really means to be happy
This raises the question of what it really means to be happy
That raises the question of what being happy really means
It raises the question of what it really means to be happy
That begs the question of what it really means to be happy
That raises the question of what happiness really means

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Raise" takes an object (raise a question); "rise" doesn't (prices rise).
commonErrors.correction_en: That raises the question of what it really means to be happy.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: English needs a subject: "what it really means" or "what happiness really means".
commonErrors.correction_en: That raises the question of what it really means to be happy.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a general statement.
accepted: Money can't buy happiness but it certainly helps

exercises.instruction_pt: Answer in one or two minutes. Stay at the level of ideas, using examples only to support them.
exercises.prompt_en: Many people say that the more we have, the less we appreciate. Do you think abundance makes us take things for granted?
guidelines_pt: Define the key idea: "By abundance, I mean...".
Give one counterexample or a paradox.

teacher.goal_pt: Recycle articles with abstract nouns and key abstract vocabulary.
prompts: What does a good friendship boil down to?
What do people take for granted?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "A vida é curta demais para isso."
accepted: Life is too short for that
Life's too short for that
Life is too short for this
Life is way too short for that
Life is far too short for that

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A vida" in general is "Life", with no article.
"Curta demais" is "too short": "too" goes before the adjective.

exercises.sentence: In the end, it all boils down ___ communication.
accepted: to

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The phrasal verb is "boil down to".
commonErrors.correction_en: In the end, it all boils down to communication.

options: The nature is beautiful in Brazil.
A nature is beautiful in Brazil.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Nature", like "life", "love" and "freedom", takes no article in a general sense.

exercises.prompt: Ultimately, it's a matter of perspective.
accepted: Ultimately, it's a matter of perspective
Ultimately, it is a matter of perspective
